correctness.rationale: From the published distance-regular intersection array and adjacency spectrum derive exact distance-polynomial relations and all four powered-distance eigenbranches. The 2-branch is strictly negative, the -3 branch is at most -17/27 for p>=0 by a global cubic bound, and the -1 branch increases through zero uniquely at 3^p-2^p=1/4. Hence the precise interval, multiplicity-10 endpoint, Gram rank 25 and Schoenberg Gaussian-kernel characterization all follow analytically. The included executable independently reconstructs the graph and checks 1296 intersection identities, polynomial equalities, adjacency spectrum and five full numerical powered-distance spectra plus explicit rook-clique reconstruction and ten exact integer contrast eigenvector identities; finite checks supplement the proof.

value.rationale: The Sylvester graph is a canonical unique distance-transitive 36-point geometry, so the exact supremal p-negative-type exponent is a natural invariant, not a contrived slice. The sharp universal range of its homogeneous Gaussian radial kernels and the geometrically explicit ten-dimensional row/column contrast endpoint kernel causing a drop from 35 to 25 in squared-Euclidean embedding dimension are substantial, interpretable geometric phenomena. The claim is a complete finite homogeneous classification with a nontrivial real-power threshold and is not presented as a family-wide theorem.
